questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Degrees Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
questions.worked_solution:
First, we recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for cosine with $u=x$ and $v={180}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-{180}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{180}^{∘}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{180}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (-1)+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot 0 \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Radians Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
questions.worked_solution:
First, we recall the sum formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for cosine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{5\pi }{3}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+\frac{5\pi }{3}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3})-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{3}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{1}{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
